rules.title: PDSPrj is ZIP-style container
rules.rule: .pdsprj files begin with PK and contain internal project files such as PROJECT.XML, ROOT.DSN, ROOT.CDB, and SCRIPTS/PWRRAILS.DAT.

rules.title: ROOT.DSN controls visual object existence
rules.rule: Components visible in ROOT.DSN appear in Proteus even if ROOT.CDB is missing entries; CDB-only components do not create visible schematic objects.

rules.title: ROOT.CDB controls resistor values and references
rules.rule: For existing resistors, ROOT.CDB is authoritative for value and reference designator. ROOT.DSN display metadata can be normalized from ROOT.CDB on open/save.

rules.title: Terminal labels live in ROOT.DSN
rules.rule: INPUT, OUTPUT, POWER, and GROUND terminal objects and labels are stored in ROOT.DSN. Terminal-only changes do not alter ROOT.CDB.

rules.title: Topology is ROOT.DSN-controlled
rules.rule: Series/parallel/ladder topology changes are represented in ROOT.DSN through terminal labels, wire stubs, and object layout. ROOT.CDB can remain identical across different topologies with the same component refs/values.

rules.title: ROOT.CDB must exist
rules.rule: Removing ROOT.CDB entirely causes fatal Proteus/ISIS failure. A generator must include ROOT.CDB, even if minimal.

rules.title: PWRRAILS.DAT unchanged in early terminal/passive tests
rules.rule: Visible VCC/GND terminals and resistor networks did not modify SCRIPTS/PWRRAILS.DAT. For early generator versions, copy this file unchanged from a template.

rules.title: V9 resistor generator uses linked endpoint groups
rules.rule: For generated resistor networks, emit matching input/output terminal records, a resistor visual record, and two short-wire records with consistent link suffixes and only one final terminator at the end of the object stream.

rules.title: V9 resistor generation uses E001 as base
rules.rule: Use the blank E001 project as the .pdsprj container base for resistor generation. Donor projects may provide byte-record templates, but generated outputs replace ROOT.CDB and ROOT.DSN and copy PROJECT.XML/PWRRAILS from E001.

rules.title: Power and ground endpoint terminals are label-width constrained
rules.rule: For the locked resistor V9 method, use two-character labels such as V0 and G0. Power bridge labels and resistor terminal labels remain two-character; $TERGROUND is safe as a right endpoint replacement for $TEROUTPUT.

rules.title: Resistor visual rotation field
rules.rule: In the V9 resistor visual record, the four bytes after the final model placement x/y pair store rotation as a signed tenths-of-degrees value in the low 16 bits. 0 is horizontal; -900 is vertical down. Vertical generation must rotate terminal/wire endpoint positions along the same axis.

rules.title: Standalone visual wires are disabled in production resistor generation
evidence: user reported VGDVC.dll errors on parallel-and-later visual-wire cases
rules.rule: Do not emit standalone layout.visual_wires in the production resistor generator. Parse and record them as skipped until a Proteus-created donor establishes VGDVC-safe standalone wire records.

rules.title: Power nodes use donor-derived output bridge
rules.rule: The main resistor generator must emit one donor-derived $TERPOWER -> $TEROUTPUT(V0) bridge for the power node. Powered resistor endpoints stay ordinary $TERINPUT(V0) terminals so same-name terminal topology connects them to the bridge.

rules.title: Dense resistor layouts are stretched before generation
evidence: user reported overlapped generated resistor circuits
rules.rule: Treat manual component coordinates as placement hints. If repeated x/y positions are closer than the safe V9 grid, stretch them before emitting ROOT.DSN so terminal records, short wires, and resistor visual bodies do not overlap. The current production safe grid is 2540000 internal units on both x and y.

rules.title: Resistor generator is locked as main for current scope
rules.rule: Use src/proteusgen/resistor_v9.py as the main resistor generator. Do not reintroduce direct $TERPOWER resistor endpoints or standalone production visual wires. New component work starts with capacitor support.

rules.title: Capacitor work stays temporary until Proteus accepts guarded diagnostics
rules.rule: Free capacitor multi-component generation using CAP_T01 visual cores and cap3-derived CDB/object expansion is user-accepted. V10 confirms the manual donor outputs-first order opens for exact, translated, renamed, and three-cap terminal-attached cases. V11 confirms the same method scales to 6C and 21C terminal-label networks. Keep the capacitor generator temporary until the V13 wider-spacing requested 15 capacitor-network pack with real power/ground terminals is Proteus accepted.

rules.title: Manual two-terminal-cap donor uses outputs-first object order
rules.rule: The user-made two-terminal-capacitor donor object chunk is ordered as: header, all $TEROUTPUT records, then each $TERINPUT/CAPACITOR/left-wire/right-wire group. Every non-final right-wire record is 49 bytes, omitting the usual trailing terminator byte; the final right-wire record is 50 bytes and ends with FF.

rules.title: Mixed resistor/capacitor passive generation is locked
rules.rule: Use src/proteusgen/mixed_passive.py as the main mixed resistor/capacitor generator for the current scope. The locked object stream order is header, one power bridge, capacitor output array, capacitor groups, resistor input array, resistor output array, separator, resistor groups. Use a 2540000 internal-unit safe grid and shift duplicate positions so components are not generated on top of each other.

rules.title: Inductor generation requires controlled donors before coding
evidence: BIG06 inductor/source empty-CDB trial opened/saved/simulated but is not a controlled donor
rules.rule: Do not infer inductor object bytes from unrelated corpus scans. Use the user-created E001-based inductor donors as record templates, then test the same terminal-first method used for resistor/capacitor generation.

rules.title: Inductor V1 donor object order
rules.rule: The first inductor V1 generator used the user-created three-terminal-inductor donor order, but all V1 generated outputs caused VGDVC.dll errors. Do not reuse V1 as positive evidence. Initial diff against the known-good two-terminal donor shows the first mutation is the terminal/component link suffix sequence; V2 must preserve donor REALIND link suffix bytes before testing further mutations.

rules.title: Inductor V2 starts with exact donor controls
rules.rule: Exact inductor donor repacks, exact donor object chunks inserted into E001, suffix-preserved single-inductor mutation, renamed/translated single-inductor mutation, and exact power/ground donor insertion work in Proteus 8.13. The generated three-inductor V2 T7 case failed, so multi-inductor generation must not be promoted from V2.

rules.title: Inductor multi-generation needs per-index diagnostics
rules.rule: For multi-inductor generation, preserve the REALIND visual record for each donor index rather than selecting only by visible value length. V3 confirms exact per-index rebuild, text mutation with donor geometry, rigid donor-geometry translation, renamed rigid translation, and formula-coordinate rebuild with per-index REALIND templates all open in Proteus 8.13.

rules.title: Inductor power/ground generation remains lock-candidate
rules.rule: Do not prepend the generic passive $TERPOWER -> $TEROUTPUT(V0) bridge before generated REALIND groups. V4 T1, T2, T3, and T5 opened partially then reported bad object record; V4 T4 gave an ISIS.dll error. The visible result showed a detached power bridge plus a separate V0 input label, so generic passive bridge ordering is rejected for inductors.

rules.title: Inductor power/ground must preserve donor04 order
rules.rule: The accepted inductor_04 power/ground donor order is input terminal, REALIND, trimmed left wire, power terminal, output terminal, bridge wire, ground terminal, final ground wire. V5 confirms exact donor04 chunk controls plus small ref/value/internal-node mutations work when preserving this order.

rules.title: Inductor promotion was premature and is demoted to temporary
rules.rule: Do not treat src/proteusgen/inductor.py or the generate-inductors CLI as main/locked. The current inductor implementation is copied to tools/proteus_generation/2026-06-01/inductor_temp_from_premature_main. The V6 6/21, V7 requested-15, and R/C/L V1 packs all failed in Proteus, so inductor promotion is blocked until new larger inductor donor evidence is supplied.

rules.title: Inductor donor03 does not extrapolate past three components
rules.rule: The accepted three-inductor V3 donor can be used only within its known three-slot scope. Repeating donor suffixes or extending suffixes from the third donor slot failed for six and twenty-one inductor generated projects. Do not generate larger inductor networks until a Proteus-created six-or-more-inductor donor provides the real object order and link/suffix pattern.

rules.title: Six-inductor donor uses sequential groups
rules.rule: The six-inductor donor object chunk is ordered as six repeated $TERINPUT/$TEROUTPUT/REALIND/left-wire/right-wire groups, not as the three-inductor donor order. The capacitor-family trim rule does apply: non-final right-wire records are 49 bytes and the final right-wire is 50 bytes. User testing confirmed V8 exact controls, six/21 generated sequential cases, the outputs-first probe, and the sequential power/ground bridge probe worked; prefer donor05 sequential order for the next inductor topology packs.

rules.title: Requested inductor topology packs stay temporary until user-opened
rules.rule: Generate requested multi-inductor V0/G0 topology packs from the accepted donor05 sequential method and donor-derived V0 bridge. Do not promote inductor code to main until the requested 15 inductor circuits and the later R/C/L mixed circuits are user-accepted.

rules.title: R/C/L mixed generation uses accepted V8 inductors
applies_to: mixed passive R/C/L temporary V2 method
rules.rule: Do not reuse the failed R/C/L V1 inductor composition or the V2 R/C-then-L-last object order. V3 confirms capacitor+inductor can work when the capacitor-family block precedes the inductor block or uses joined outputs-first ordering. V5 confirms free R/L/C component records can coexist and be inserted into E001. V6 shows terminal-attached C and L work around a free resistor. V7 T02-T07 show a terminal-attached resistor can coexist with free L/C when the resistor block is placed last/final. V8 shows this does not extend to terminal C/L plus final R: only the free L/C control T01 worked, and no-power all-terminal T02 failed. V9 then showed all generated minimal terminal R+L order/index/suffix variants failed. Stop generated guessing at this boundary and require a Proteus-created terminal-attached resistor plus terminal-attached inductor donor before producing more R/C/L topology packs.

rules.title: Manual RLC donor is a family-order donor, not a topology donor
applies_to: mixed passive R/C/L temporary V5 method
rules.rule: The user-supplied rlc_manual_donor object chunk contains free component records in L1, R1, C1 order with matching ROOT.CDB entries, but contains no $TERINPUT, $TEROUTPUT, $TERPOWER, $TERGROUND, or WIRE records. User testing confirmed V5 T01-T04 donor controls work, so this donor is valid evidence for free component coexistence, DSN header compatibility, and CDB metadata. It is not evidence for generated terminal topology: V5 T05-T10 all failed.

rules.title: RLC terminal topology must be isolated by family
applies_to: mixed passive R/C/L temporary V6 method
rules.rule: V6 identifies the family boundary: terminal-attached L with free R/C works, terminal-attached C with free L/R works, terminal-attached C+L with free R works in disconnected and connected forms, but terminal-attached R fails in every tested combination containing an inductor. Do not generate R/C/L topologies with the current V9 resistor terminal record until resistor-specific diagnostics pass.

rules.title: RLC terminal resistor suffix and order must be tested before topology generation
applies_to: mixed passive R/C/L temporary V7 method
rules.rule: V7 T02-T07 show terminal R can coexist with free L/C if free L/C records are first and the resistor terminal block is final. The specific ordinal/index/suffix policy was not the deciding factor because all tested variants T02-T07 worked. V8 shows that this rule does not solve all-terminal R/C/L: only T01 worked, and T02 without power/ground failed. Do not infer full all-terminal R/C/L support from the V7 free-L/C result.

rules.title: RLC terminal resistor final ordering is positive only for free L/C scope
applies_to: mixed passive R/C/L temporary V7/V8 method
rules.rule: When a project contains free capacitor and inductor donor records, a terminal-attached resistor works if its complete terminal/resistor/wire block is the final object block. This is not sufficient when the inductor is terminal-attached: V8 T02 failed without power/ground. Do not proceed to larger R/C/L topologies until a minimal terminal R plus terminal L case works or a manual donor reveals the native Proteus R/L object order.

rules.title: RLC active blocker is terminal resistor plus terminal inductor
applies_to: mixed passive R/C/L temporary V8/V9 method
rules.rule: The first failing condition is not power/ground, shared terminal labels, or large component count. V8 T02 failed with disconnected labels and no power/ground. Existing positive evidence covers terminal C+L with free R and terminal R with free L/C. V9 directly tested minimal terminal R+L order, index, and suffix hypotheses; the user reported none worked. Do not generate larger mixed R/C/L circuits until a clean Proteus-created terminal R+L donor is analyzed.

rules.title: Manual terminal R+L donor is required
rules.rule: The current corpus now includes Proteus-created terminal R+L donors. The disconnected donor is the primary mutation template: its native object order is header, both inputs, L output+REALIND+wires, then R output+RESISTOR+wires. Do not promote mixed R/C/L until V10 donor controls and donor-native generated cases are user-accepted in Proteus.

rules.title: Native terminal R+L order uses inputs-first mixed groups
rules.rule: For a Proteus-created disconnected terminal R+L project, ROOT.DSN object data is not normal resistor V9 order and not inductor sequential group order. It is header, two $TERINPUT records, then the inductor's $TEROUTPUT/REALIND/left-wire/right-wire group, then the resistor's $TEROUTPUT/boundary-byte/RESISTOR/left-wire/right-wire group. V10 tests whether this native order is safe to mutate.
